newsitem.title: GERMANY: Hypo-Bank has no sign of large share buy.
newsitem.headline: Hypo-Bank has no sign of large share buy.

text.p: Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG chief excecutive Eberhard Martini said on Wednesday that he had no knowledge of any single investor amassing a stake in the bank.
"I think our shareholder structure is unchanged," Martini told a news conference, adding "there is no sign anywhere that a parcel of shares has been bought."

Hypo-Bank shares have risen sharply recently on speculation that the bank may be a target for a takeover bid as part of an expected consolidation in Germany's overcrowded banking sector. Hypo-Bank is Germany's fifth largest listed bank.

Martini also said a hostile takeover of his bank would cost about 20 billion marks, a prohibitively high price. "I can't imagine that someone would pay this for a bank," he said, adding that the market capitalisation of Germany's big banks had reached "unbelievable volumes".

On Tuesday, Martin Kohlhaussen the chairman of Germany's third largest bank, Commerzbank, also said the price for his bank was extremely high, shrugging off similar talk that Commerzbank might be an attractive takeover target.
